messages.author: e302709dad51d37a
messages.subject: Faster Simulation Processing
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to run a simulation several times over and it is taking a long time.

I tried using the mclapply function from the parallel package, but it function about the same as a regular old for loop. I guess you can only use 1 core if you are running on Windows.

I can supply my code if necessary, but do you have any ideas/tips?

Best,
John

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Faster Simulation Processing
parts:
El jue., 16 ago. 2018 a las 15:24, John Redmond
(<john.re...@gmail.com>) escribió:

>
> Hi,
>
> I am trying to run a simulation several times over and it is taking a long time.
>
> I tried using the mclapply function from the parallel package, but it function about the same as a regular old for loop. I guess you can only use 1 core if you are running on Windows.
>
> I can supply my code if necessary, but do you have any ideas/tips?

'mclapply' relies on POSIX process forking, so it doesn't work on
Windows. The parallel package has other facilities to support
parallelism though, such as 'makeCluster', but the setup requires a
little bit more boilerplate (see the docs).

Apart from that, there are many other solutions to enable parallelism
in R, and a good starting point is the ''High-Performance and Parallel
Computing with R" task view:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/views/HighPerformanceComputing.html

One of the most recent and promising packages is the 'future' package
by Henrik Bengtsson. It has several nice vignettes to help the user
quickly grasp the concepts and usage.

Iñaki


>
> Best,
> John
